home-remodeling.local_heading: Local knowledge, from the Cove westward
intro_paragraphs: Deerfield Beach keeps its best housing stock east of Federal Highway and out of sight. The Cove holds roughly a thousand single-family homes threaded through about twenty finger canals off the Intracoastal, and a single street can run from a 1960s terrazzo-floored ranch to a glass-walled rebuild finished last spring. Head west and Deer Creek spreads over 600 acres and fifteen subdivisions of homes built from 1974 onward, with Villages of Hillsboro, Coquina Lakes and Independence Bay filling the gaps. Owners in all of them ask for the same thing: the layout opened, the systems replaced, the storm exposure solved in one pass.

Permits run through the City of Deerfield Beach Building Division on NE 2nd Avenue, which takes submittals online through GeoCivix and through ePermitsOneStop, the site the city shares with Broward County so county reviews ride along. Inspection requests filed by 3 p.m. are picked up the next business day, and every residential application needs the city's HOA affidavit, association or no association. Above the city sits the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which reviews local code amendments, issues formal interpretations, and certifies the officials and inspectors who show up at your door. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so every opening carries HVHZ product approval.

Behind that sit 20-plus years of South Florida construction and more than 150 remodels and additions delivered, all of them permitted and inspected. On a whole-house job the scope is settled in writing before the first wall comes down, a supervisor is on site every day, and the rooms we are not touching get treated as finished goods — masked, papered, swept nightly. One team carries the work from estimate through final inspection and warranty. That means one number to call at seven in the morning, and one person who cannot pass the question along.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to gut and remodel a house in Deerfield Beach?
faqs.a: Yes. Anything touching structure, plumbing, electrical, mechanical or exterior openings goes through the city's Building Division for plan review, then a sequence of inspections. Deerfield Beach also wants the owner's signature on the application and a completed HOA affidavit for every residential permit. Skipping the process is a short-term saving with a long tail: unpermitted work surfaces during a sale, during an insurance claim, and during the next permit you apply for.

faqs.q: What is the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, and does it affect my project?
faqs.a: It is the county-level code body that sits above every Broward building department. Established under the county charter, it reviews local amendments to the Florida Building and Fire Prevention codes, issues formal interpretations of code sections, hears appeals of building and fire official decisions, and certifies the building officials, plans examiners and inspectors working in Broward cities. You will never sit in front of it. Its practical effect is that inspection standards stay consistent from Deerfield Beach to Weston.

faqs.q: My Cove house sits in a flood zone. Does that cap what I can spend?
faqs.a: It shapes the project rather than capping it. Much of the canal side falls in FEMA AE or AH zones, and the federal substantial improvement rule compares the cost of your work against the market value of the structure; cross fifty percent and the whole building must be brought into flood compliance. Deerfield Beach participates in the Community Rating System and publishes elevation certificates on its map, so we run that math before design, not during permitting.

faqs.q: How long does a whole-home remodel take here?
faqs.a: Design and engineering usually take a couple of months, permitting adds time that varies with how complete the submittal is, and construction on a full house commonly runs six months to a year depending on structural work and how much of it is custom. Canal-lot projects with flood-elevation questions run longer on the front end. You get a written schedule with the estimate, and daily supervision exists partly to defend it.

faqs.q: What should a full gut in Deerfield Beach cost?
faqs.a: A finish-level refresh and a full gut with new service, new plumbing and new openings are not the same species of project, so a single number would be theater. What we commit to is a fixed written scope with real allowances instead of placeholders, so the figure you sign is the figure you pay barring documented surprises. PGX is a high-end contractor and rarely the lowest of three bids. Clients hire us for the certainty.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the survey, the plans, or just the list of things that annoy you. You leave with a written scope and a real number, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Deerfield Beach kitchen remodeling that moves the cooking wall toward the canal, with real cabinetry and stone. PGX Builders, (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: A kitchen worth the canal view
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and layout changes for Deerfield Beach kitchens, from Cove canal houses to Deer Creek golf-course homes. Fully permitted, inspected, and run by a licensed general contractor who is on site daily.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Why Cove kitchens nearly always move
intro_paragraphs: Most Cove kitchens were built facing the wrong way. The 1960s and 70s canal houses put the kitchen at the front of the plan, boxed off from the living room, while the water sat behind a wall of jalousies and a laundry closet. So a serious kitchen remodel in Deerfield Beach is usually a relocation: cooking moves to the back of the house, an island lands where a partition stood, and the sink finally looks at the dock. Out in Deer Creek, Villages of Hillsboro and Coquina Lakes the problem is different: 1980s builder kitchens with dropped soffits, a peninsula, and nowhere for a second oven.

Because a real kitchen touches plumbing, electrical, gas and often structure, it is permitted work through the Deerfield Beach Building Division. Applications go in through the city portal with the HOA affidavit the city requires on every residential permit, and in a condominium the association's approval letter goes in with them. Before demolition, Broward County wants its asbestos statement of responsibility and the certificate of submittal that comes back with it. Enlarge the window over the sink and you have added an HVHZ product approval and a window schedule matched to the design pressures on that elevation.

Kitchens here get built in the order a cabinetmaker would ask for. Field dimensions get verified against shop drawings before anything is released to the shop, stone is templated on installed boxes rather than off a plan, and appliance rough-ins are set from the model numbers you actually bought rather than the ones you were considering in March. Scope is fixed in writing, a supervisor runs the site daily, and the rest of the house lives behind sealed dust walls with a protected path to the door. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072, 20-plus years in South Florida.

faqs.q: Does a kitchen remodel need a permit in Deerfield Beach?
faqs.a: If you are moving plumbing, changing electrical, adding gas or opening a wall, then yes, through the city's Building Division with inspections along the way. Swapping a dishwasher into an existing hookup or repainting does not require one. In a condominium the city is stricter still: unit work requires a licensed contractor and a permit card posted where an inspector can read it from outside the door. Interior painting and floor covering are about the only exceptions.

faqs.q: Can the wall between my kitchen and living room come out in a Cove house?
faqs.a: Usually, but not casually. These houses are concrete block with poured tie-beams, and the interior partitions vary between non-bearing stud walls and real load paths. An engineer determines which you have, sizes the beam and details the bearing, and that drawing becomes part of the permit set. Wide openings on the canal side sometimes need a column you did not plan on. We tell you the structural answer before you commit to the rendering.

faqs.q: My condo association has its own rules. What does the city need from them?
faqs.a: Deerfield Beach requires an HOA affidavit with every residential permit application, so association sign-off and city permitting move together rather than in sequence. Boards here typically add their own conditions: approved work hours, service-elevator windows, protection of common corridors, insurance certificates from every trade, and sound-attenuation requirements under new flooring. We assemble that package early, because the association calendar is usually the slower of the two.

faqs.q: How long does a custom kitchen take start to finish?
faqs.a: Cabinetry sets the clock. Made-to-order packages take months to fabricate, which is why we release them early and hold demolition until delivery is realistic — nobody should live around a gutted kitchen waiting on a truck. On-site construction typically runs a couple of months, longer where a structural opening or a relocated gas line is involved. Think in seasons rather than weekends and the schedule will treat you well.

faqs.q: What does a high-end kitchen cost in Deerfield Beach?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone lead the budget, appliances follow closely, and the range widens fast with selections. Structural openings and panel upgrades move it further. Rather than quote a vague per-foot figure, we walk the space, write a specification, and price against it, so you are comparing real scopes. If the deciding factor is the lowest number on the table, we will say so early and shake hands anyway.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send photos or open the door and show us. You get a fixed-scope written estimate and honest lead times, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Bathroom remodeling in Deerfield Beach, FL — primary suites, frameless glass, flood-tested waterproofing in canal homes and oceanfront condos. (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: The bath the Cove house needed
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless glass, freestanding tubs and stone for Deerfield Beach houses and oceanfront condos. Pans flood-tested before tile, every permit pulled, every inspection kept, one licensed contractor accountable for the result.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Small original baths, salt air, slab floors
intro_paragraphs: A 1965 Cove house came with a hall bath, a tub you step over, and a primary bath the size of a good closet. A 1980s Deer Creek home came with a garden tub, a glass-block window, and a shower built for someone with no elbows. Both get the same treatment now: the hall bath and an adjoining closet or bedroom combined into a genuine primary suite, a low-curb or curbless shower, a freestanding tub where the floor supports one, and stone that will not stain in the first week. Condo owners over on Deerfield Beach Island chase the same result in tighter space.

The Deerfield Beach Building Division permits bath work, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections before anything gets closed up, which is exactly when a waterproofing mistake is still cheap. In a condominium the city requires a licensed contractor, the HOA affidavit with the application, and the permit card displayed where an inspector can read it from outside your unit. Older beachfront towers also sit inside Florida's milestone inspection era: buildings of three stories and up reach their first structural milestone at thirty years, and the local building official may require it at twenty-five near the coast. Boards have grown curious about anything touching a slab.

It is the smallest room in the house and the least forgiving one. Pans get flood-tested and held, slopes get verified with a level rather than a hopeful eye, and heavy glass hangs on blocking installed for that purpose during framing. Niches are waterproofed like everything else, because that is where the shortcuts hide. Exhaust goes outside the building, not into a soffit to condense. Scope in writing, supervision daily, protection on every finished surface between the front door and the work zone. Lic. CGC1539072, licensed and insured, permitted and inspected without exception.

faqs.q: Are permits required for a bathroom remodel in Deerfield Beach?
faqs.a: For anything past cosmetics, yes. Relocating or replacing plumbing, altering circuits, and changing ventilation all require permits through the city's Building Division, with inspections before walls close. Treat that as insurance rather than friction: it means an inspector verified your rough plumbing and waterproofing while they were still visible. We pull the permits, book the inspections, and hand you the closed-out records at the end.

faqs.q: I own an oceanfront condo. What will the association and the city each want?
faqs.a: The city wants a licensed contractor, an HOA affidavit with the permit application, and the permit card posted visibly at your unit until the job closes out. The association typically wants insurance certificates, approved work hours, service-elevator reservations, protected corridors, and a plan for water shutoffs. In buildings inside their milestone inspection window, boards also scrutinize anything involving slab penetrations or plumbing risers. We collect all of it before demolition.

faqs.q: Can I get a curbless shower in a 1960s Cove house?
faqs.a: Often, but the slab decides. Recessing the pan means saw-cutting concrete and sometimes relocating the waste line, which is straightforward when the drain run cooperates and expensive when it does not. Where the structure genuinely will not allow it, a low-profile curb with a correctly sloped pan and a linear drain gets you most of the look. We investigate before design so the answer arrives early rather than mid-demolition.

faqs.q: How long will the bathroom be out of service?
faqs.a: A full primary bath typically runs several weeks on site once materials are staged, and the honest driver is lead time on tile, slabs, glass and fixtures rather than labor. Custom glass is measured after tile is set, so allow a couple of weeks at the end for fabrication. We sequence so a second bathroom stays functional and never demolish anything we cannot make progress on the following day.

faqs.q: What should a primary bath remodel cost at this level?
faqs.a: Stone, glass and fixtures set the visible budget; new drains, supply lines, waterproofing and ventilation set the invisible one, and that second half is the part people underestimate. Instead of quoting a fantasy range, we open the walls conceptually with you, scope what the building actually needs, and put a fixed number in writing. We compete on finish quality and certainty, not on being the cheapest bid received.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and tell us what fails you daily. A written scope and a firm number follow, in English o en español.

home-additions.meta_description: Grow a Deerfield Beach house up or out: second stories over block, rear extensions, in-law suites. Elevation and permits handled. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Grow the house, keep the address
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, garage conversions and in-law suites across Deerfield Beach — engineered foundations and tie-beams, drawings the city will approve, and a licensed general contractor supervising the site every day.
home-additions.local_heading: Adding on between the canals and the fairways
intro_paragraphs: Cove lots are wide but shallow, and the canal claims the back of the property, so additions there tend to go up or sideways instead of straight out. A second story over a 1960s block ranch is the signature project, closely followed by enclosing a carport or pushing a primary suite toward the street side. West of the interstate the geometry relaxes: in Deer Creek, Coquina Lakes and The Waterways the classic job is a rear family room, a home office wing, or an in-law suite off the garage. Independence Bay and Villages of Hillsboro owners mostly add conditioned space to lots that were never short on land.

Every review layer in Deerfield Beach shows up at once on an addition. Zoning comes first: the city publishes single-family setback requirements, and the Land Development Code governs lot coverage and height before anyone talks about beam sizes. The Building Division then reviews structure, and a Broward-certified plans examiner signs it, because the county Board of Rules and Appeals certifies the officials and inspectors staffing every Broward building department. On a canal lot your FEMA zone drives finished floor elevation and the fifty-percent substantial improvement threshold, and the city's Community Rating System participation means elevation data is public and easy to pull.

New foundations tied to fifty-year-old ones are the part of an addition nobody photographs and everybody eventually feels. We underpin where the soil report says to, match block coursing and stucco texture so the seam disappears, and dry the new roof into the old one before opening anything we cannot close by evening. The occupied half of the house keeps power, water and a working kitchen wherever sequencing allows. Fixed written scope, one supervisor on site daily, and a single accountable team from the feasibility sketch to final inspection and warranty.

scope_items.name: Rear and side extensions
scope_items.desc: Family rooms, primary suites and offices pushed into the yard, with the foundation, tie-beam and roof work drawn, engineered and permitted together.

scope_items.name: Carports and garages enclosed
scope_items.desc: Enclosing covered parking as insulated, conditioned space with HVHZ openings and extended mechanicals, permitted so an appraiser can actually count it.

scope_items.name: A suite for family
scope_items.desc: A private wing with its own bath, sitting area and a small galley, built to code and massed so the addition reads as original from the street.

scope_items.name: Footings, steel and elevation
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings and structural steel, plus the finished floor elevation your flood zone requires rather than the one the original slab happens to sit at.

faqs.q: Does Deerfield Beach have a design review board for single-family additions?
faqs.a: Not in the way some coastal cities do. The city's Community Appearance Board reviews exterior aesthetics for multi-family, commercial and industrial properties, so a house addition is not going before an architectural board the way it would in some South Florida cities. What governs you instead is zoning: setbacks, height and lot coverage. In Deer Creek, Independence Bay and similar communities, an HOA architectural committee adds its own submittal package and its own calendar.

faqs.q: Will flood rules stop me from adding onto a Cove canal house?
faqs.a: Rarely stop, frequently shape. Canal properties commonly fall in FEMA AE or AH zones, where new conditioned space must meet flood construction standards and the federal substantial improvement rule compares your investment against the structure's market value. Cross fifty percent and the entire building must be brought into compliance, which can turn an addition into a broader project. We run that analysis with your elevation certificate before design, so nobody discovers it at plan review.

faqs.q: Can my 1960s block house carry a second story?
faqs.a: Many can, some need reinforcement, and an engineer settles it rather than a contractor's instinct. Existing footings, block condition and the original tie-beam get evaluated first; where capacity falls short, new columns, thickened footings and upgraded beams get designed in. Occasionally the honest recommendation is a ground-floor extension instead, and we will say so with numbers attached rather than defend a design that costs you more to build.

faqs.q: How long does an addition take from first drawing to move-in?
faqs.a: Front-load your expectations. Design and structural engineering usually take a couple of months, HOA architectural review adds its own cycle where it applies, permitting varies with submittal completeness, and construction runs several months more, longer for a second story, which involves temporary roofing and a house partially open to weather. A year from first meeting to furnished room is a realistic frame for a substantial addition.

faqs.q: Is adding on smarter than buying a bigger house in Deerfield Beach?
faqs.a: Often, if the location is the reason you are here. Dockage, an ocean-access canal or a Deer Creek fairway lot is not something you replace by moving three miles west, and an addition buys exactly the space you are missing while preserving what you already like. It is still months of real construction, so it rewards owners planning to stay. We give a candid feasibility read before you spend money on drawings.

home-additions.cta_sub: Bring the survey if you have one. We will talk setbacks, structure, flood elevation and honest numbers, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.local_heading: Where the county gets involved out back
intro_paragraphs: The backyard is the entire point of a Cove house. Twenty-odd finger canals mean most of these lots end at a seawall with a dock, and the ground between the slider and the water earns its keep twelve months a year. So the projects run large: a covered terrace with a full summer kitchen, a pool deck rebuilt in shell stone, a pergola shading the western exposure that makes four o'clock unbearable. Inland, around Deer Creek, Crystal Lake and Eastway Park, it is fairway and lake frontage instead of dockage, with the same appetite for an outdoor room that still works in August.

Exterior work is where a Deerfield Beach project stops being purely a city matter. Structures and the gas, water and electrical serving a summer kitchen are permitted through the city's Building Division, and the city's landscape code and tree programs govern what comes out of the ground. Anything in, on or under surface waters, including seawall repair or replacement, a new dock, dredging and mangrove trimming, is licensed separately by Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program, and ePermitsOneStop is where the two tracks meet. Over on Deerfield Beach Island, sea turtle nesting runs early March through October and exterior lighting has to behave accordingly.

Outdoor construction fails in two places, water and wind, so that is where the money goes. Terraces get pitched away from the house with the slider threshold detailed properly, pergola and trellis footings are engineered for uplift instead of guessed at by post size, and marine-grade stainless, sealed dense stone and coastal-rated hardware get specified wherever salt air actually reaches. Re-roofing gets sequenced so a new covered structure ties into new roofing rather than the last owner's. Fixed scope in writing, a site swept clean each evening, and crews who understand that a gated Deer Creek entrance has rules.
outdoor-living.scope_heading: Backyard work, from grill to seawall
outdoor-living.scope_intro: From a single terrace to a whole rebuilt waterfront yard, each element gets designed, permitted and built as one coordinated project.

scope_items.desc: Permitted gas, water and electrical runs, weather-rated cabinetry and counters, and ventilation that works under a solid roof instead of only in a photograph.

scope_items.name: Seawalls, docks, county review
scope_items.desc: Shoreline and dock scopes coordinated through Broward County's aquatic and wetland licensing alongside the city permit, with the schedule built around both reviews.

scope_items.name: Driveways, decks and drainage
scope_items.desc: Pavers, shell stone and finished concrete on a base that will not settle, pitched to move a genuine South Florida downpour away from the slab.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint, impact openings
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration, control-joint and stucco repair, repainting, and HVHZ-approved doors and sliders replacing the aluminum units the salt air already retired.

faqs.q: Do I need a county approval for seawall or dock work on my Cove canal?
faqs.a: Yes, in addition to the city permit. Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program licenses work in, on or under surface waters: seawalls, docks, dredge and fill, mangrove trimming. The county has also published regional guidance on seawall standards intended to keep tidal barriers effective as sea levels rise. Practically, that means two review tracks and a schedule that respects both. We manage the sequencing rather than handing you a phone number.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for a summer kitchen or a pergola?
faqs.a: For both. The structure needs a building permit with engineered footings and connections rated for our wind loads, and the gas, water and electrical runs need their own trade permits and inspections. It feels like a lot of paper for a grill and a roof, right up until a storm removes an unengineered pergola from someone else's yard. We fold the approvals into the contract as our work, not your homework.

faqs.q: Will the Community Appearance Board review my backyard project?
faqs.a: Not for a single-family home. The Deerfield Beach Community Appearance Board reviews exterior aesthetics for multi-family, commercial and industrial properties, so a house terrace or summer kitchen goes through building and zoning review rather than an aesthetics hearing. A condominium terrace or a building-wide exterior change is a different story, and so is any community with its own architectural committee. We confirm which path applies at the first site visit.

faqs.q: How does being on the Intracoastal change what you specify?
faqs.a: Materially. Salt-laden air off the water finds ordinary stainless, powder-coated aluminum and builder-grade hardware within a couple of seasons, so waterfront scopes get marine-grade stainless, dense stone sealed on a schedule, coated fasteners and finishes chosen for exposure rather than showroom appeal. Outdoor cabinetry in particular is where budgets get quietly cut and regretted. Specify correctly once and the terrace ages with the house instead of ahead of it.

faqs.q: What should a full outdoor living project cost?
faqs.a: What drives it is structure and utilities, not the size of the slab. A rebuilt paver terrace is one conversation; a covered outdoor room with a full summer kitchen, gas, water, electrical and engineered footings is genuinely another, and shoreline work with county licensing sits in its own category. We walk the yard, write a specification, and price against it so you are comparing real scopes rather than per-foot guesses that ignore what is under the slab.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: The city counter and the county rulebook
intro_paragraphs: The Cove has been changing hands since the 1960s, and six decades of owners leave a paper trail. Canal houses off the Intracoastal have been re-roofed, re-glazed, repiped, screened in and added to, sometimes on a permit and sometimes over a quiet long weekend. Deer Creek, Coquina Lakes and Villages of Hillsboro carry the same history in a shorter span: pool cages, carport enclosures, panel upgrades, a water heater that moved rooms. None of it evaporates. An unfinished permit stays attached to the address until somebody finishes it, and most owners meet theirs with a buyer already under contract.

Deerfield Beach is its own municipality, so permits are filed with the city's Building Division on NE 2nd Avenue and move through the GeoCivix portal, while ePermitsOneStop carries the Broward County pieces that ride alongside: asbestos notification before demolition, environmental review, the notice of commencement. Above the city sits the county Board of Rules and Appeals, the layer every Broward building department answers to, which maintains Broward's amendments to the Florida Building Code and certifies the plans examiners and inspectors who will judge your job. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so glass, doors and roofing need approved products documented in the file.

There is a difference between running paperwork and being able to build whatever the file is missing, and it usually decides how this goes. Old permits close when the work behind them is finished: a failed component replaced, a wall opened so an inspector can see the framing, an engineer's letter written for something long since covered. We read the permit history first and tell you which of the three you are facing, in writing, before you spend anything. Our supervisor is at the house when the inspector pulls up. 20-plus years in South Florida, more than 150 remodels and additions delivered, all of them permitted and inspected. Lic. CGC1539072.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: The paperwork, and the work behind it
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Half of this is a new project done correctly from the first drawing. The other half is clearing what a previous owner left open. Both go under our license.

scope_items.desc: The address history pulled, the dormant file moved into an active license, the unfinished work completed, and a final inspection signed rather than promised.

faqs.q: A title search on our Deerfield Beach house turned up an open permit. Now what?
faqs.a: It does not close with the sale. The permit stays with the property, and your title company will hold the closing while the file is open. We pull the record, confirm whether the work was ever built at all, and move the permit into an active contractor's name so it can be finished and inspected. Work now hidden behind finishes may need an engineer's letter instead of an inspector's eyes. Count on weeks rather than days, and start well before your closing date.

faqs.q: Who actually issues a building permit in Deerfield Beach?
faqs.a: The City of Deerfield Beach. This is a municipality rather than unincorporated county, so applications, plans and revisions go to the city's Building Division through GeoCivix, with ePermitsOneStop carrying the Broward County reviews that travel with them. Behind the city sits the county Board of Rules and Appeals, which maintains Broward's code amendments and certifies the officials reviewing your job. No aesthetic board stands between a house permit and issuance here; the Community Appearance Board looks at multi-family and commercial exteriors.

faqs.q: A previous owner enclosed the carport and swapped the windows with no permit. Can that be fixed?
faqs.a: Usually, and far better fixed before a buyer's inspector finds it. Unpermitted work gets legalized with as-built drawings, engineering where structure is involved, and a permit reviewed against the code in force today rather than the year the work happened. That last part bites: replacement glass has to carry High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approval, so windows that went in quietly two decades ago may not survive review. On a canal lot the value of that work also counts toward your substantial improvement math.

faqs.q: I own in an oceanfront building on Deerfield Beach Island. What applies to my unit and my building?
faqs.a: Two separate tracks. Unit work needs a licensed contractor, the HOA affidavit with the application, and a permit card posted where an inspector can read it from outside your door. The building answers to Broward's building safety inspection program, administered through the county Board of Rules and Appeals, and to Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study for condominium buildings of three stories and up. Those reports belong to a licensed engineer. We price, permit, build and close out the repairs they call for.

faqs.q: What does it cost to close out an old permit?
faqs.a: Nobody can quote that from an address, and anyone who tries is guessing. The money sits in the work, not the filing: a file that needs an inspector to look at existing framing is one number, a roof that has to come off is another species entirely. We pull the record, walk the property, and hand you a fixed written scope with real line items instead of a placeholder. City fees are what the city charges and are passed through at cost.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: First the record, then the plan
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send us the address. You will hear what Deerfield Beach has on file for the property before anyone talks about money, in English o en español.
